zh.principle: **算法**：Argon2 口令派生（Argon2）。§1 给出定性：「Argon2 is a memory-hard function [HARD].It is a streamlined design.」变体结构同段印明：「Argon2 has one primary variant, Argon2id, and two supplementary variants, Argon2d and Argon2i.」也即它不是单一函数而是一个家族，且主变体只有一个。
zh.why: 设计目标写在成本模型上：「It aims at the highest memory-filling rate and effective use of multiple computing units, while still providing defense against trade-off attacks.」衡量它的不是单次哈希的算力，而是能否把可用内存真正填满、并用多核抬高攻击者成本，同时不让时间-内存折抵占便宜。硬件取向也一并交代：「Argon2 is optimized for the x86 architecture and exploits the cache and memory organization of the recent Intel and AMD processors.」
zh.used: 选型与实现义务都在原文里。用途分工是「Argon2i uses data-independent memory access, which is preferred for password hashing and password-based key derivation.」实现层面的底线是规范性一句：「Argon2id MUST be supported by any implementation of this document, whereas Argon2d and Argon2i MAY be supported.」也即任何声称符合本文件的实现都必须支持主变体，另外两支是可选。
zh.broken: 限度由变体分工反出：Argon2d 的数据相关内存访问正是侧信道计时攻击的面，所以原文把它的适用场景限定为「with no threats from side-channel timing attacks」。文本另在一处给出彻底阻止的条件：要完全阻止所引工作的时空间折抵，趟数必须大于内存容量以 2 为底的对数减 26（这是有条件的防御，不是普遍消除），文本的说法是「providing defense against trade-off attacks」——防御而非证明不存在；Argon2i 还「makes more passes over the memory to protect from trade-off attacks」，用额外的趟数换安全性，成本因此上升。
zh.history:
版本事实：摘要段印明本文件对应哪一个算法版本 -「corresponds to version 1.3 of the Argon2 hash function.」头部信息为 Request for Comments: 9106、Category: Informational、March 2021，作者行是 Bassham 与 Liu（头部按项目口径复述于引号外）。也即 RFC 9106 标准化的是 Argon2 的 1.3 版，而不是它的原始竞赛提交版。

该条目的形式模型是 \(C=E_K(P;r),\qquad P=D_K(C)\)。输入：输入：Argon2 口令派生的公开参数、密钥/随机数与消息；变量说明：P 明文，C 密文，K 密钥，r 随机化参数。 预期输出：按 Argon2 口令派生 的规范执行后得到可验证的输出或可比较的优势界。 复算必须给出输入、步骤、输出和单位；示例只演示流程，不替代标准测试向量。

en.principle: **Algorithm**: Argon2 (Argon2 口令派生). Section 1 gives the character: "Argon2 is a memory-hard function [HARD]. It is a streamlined design." The family structure is printed in the same passage: "Argon2 has one primary variant, Argon2id, and two supplementary variants, Argon2d and Argon2i." So Argon2 is a family with exactly one primary member.
en.why: The goal is stated in cost-model terms: "It aims at the highest memory-filling rate and effective use of multiple computing units, while still providing defense against trade-off attacks." The metric is not hashes per second but how completely memory is filled and how many compute units are used, without letting time-memory trade-offs win. The hardware posture follows: "Argon2 is optimized for the x86 architecture and exploits the cache and memory organization of the recent Intel and AMD processors."
en.used:
Selection and implementation duty are both in the text. The division of labour: "Argon2i uses data-independent memory access, which is preferred for password hashing and password-based key derivation." The normative floor: "Argon2id MUST be supported by any implementation of this document, whereas Argon2d and Argon2i MAY be supported." So any implementation claiming conformance must support the primary variant; the other two are optional.

A shared name may belong to an algorithm, standard, event, person or term; this entry is responsible only for its catalogue binding and does not absorb adjacent records. If versions, regions or institutions define the name differently, the differences stay side by side.
en.broken: The limits fall out of the same division: Argon2d's data-dependent access is precisely the side-channel timing surface, which is why the text confines it to scenarios "with no threats from side-channel timing attacks". The text does claim complete prevention of one family, conditionally: to completely prevent the time-memory trade-offs of the cited work the number of passes must exceed the binary logarithm of memory minus 26 - so this entry reads the position as a conditional defence rather than a claim that trade-offs are eliminated in general - the wording is "providing defense against trade-off attacks", defence rather than proof - and Argon2i additionally "makes more passes over the memory to protect from trade-off attacks", buying safety with extra passes and therefore extra cost.
en.history: Version facts: the abstract pins the algorithm release - "corresponds to version 1.3 of the Argon2 hash function." The header prints Request for Comments: 9106, Category: Informational, March 2021, by Bassham and Liu (restated outside quotes per house rule). So RFC 9106 standardises version 1.3 of the Password-Hashing Competition winner, not its original submission.

zh: Argon2：面向口令哈希的记忆密集函数，本 RFC 对应其 1.3 版。
Argon2d：数据相关的内存访问变体，适合无侧信道计时威胁的工作量证明场景。
Argon2i：数据无关的内存访问变体，优先用于口令哈希与口令派生。
Argon2id：第一趟前半按 Argon2i、其余按 Argon2d 的主变体。
记忆密集：以填满内存的程度衡量成本的函数类型。
时间-内存折抵：Argon2 设计要压制的攻击面。
en: Argon2: the memory-hard password function this RFC specifies, corresponding to version 1.3.
Argon2d: the data-dependent memory-access variant, suited to proof-of-work without side-channel threats.
Argon2i: the data-independent memory-access variant, preferred for password hashing and PBKDF.
Argon2id: the primary variant, Argon2i for the first half of the first pass and Argon2d afterwards.
Memory-hard: a function whose cost is measured by how completely it fills memory.
Time-memory trade-off: the attack surface Argon2 aims to suppress by spending computation.
